tasks.title: makeOutboundFetch on safeGet; move Spider robots/sitemap, RobotsPolicy.fetch and access-control onto it
tasks.description: Implements ADR 0031 for the core paths (part 1 of 2; BE-104 does the checkers and the orchestrator). In packages/core/src/safe-net.ts: add an `allowPrivate` option to safeGet (private addresses accepted but still resolved once per hop and pinned; every redirect hop re-checked), and export `makeOutboundFetch(opts)` returning the checkers' `FetchFn` shape (packages/checkers/src/security-depth.ts:30): GET only, body read up to a byte cap (a body over the cap still counts as a response with its status), timeout, optional extra headers (e.g. Cookie). `allowPrivate` is derived from the run, never from request input: private allowed only when no browser guard is set (getBrowserPolicy() === null, packages/core/src/browser.ts:60; RUNNER_BETA=1 sets one). Also export a small `sameSiteUrl(url, site)` helper used for sitemap host checks. Migrate: (1) Deterministic Spider sitemap seeding (deterministic-spider.ts:405-459) from context.request.get to an injectable `outboundFetch` option defaulting to makeOutboundFetch; a robots.txt `Sitemap:` line and a sitemap `<loc>` naming another host are logged (debugLog 'crawl') and skipped (today `Sitemap:` lines are pushed with no host check, :416-418). (2) RobotsPolicy.fetch (competitive/robots.ts:48-56) from Node fetch to a FetchFn parameter defaulting to makeOutboundFetch({ allowPrivate: false }), so callers (discovery-agent.ts:477, safe-crawler.ts:167, runner routes/plan.ts:631) keep their signature; missing/unreachable robots.txt still means allow all. (3) access-control contextFetcher (access-control.ts:176-183) from context.request.get to makeOutboundFetch with the context's cookies as a Cookie header and maxRedirects 0, same AccessFetcher signature so orchestrator.ts is untouched. Unit tests use injected NetDeps (no real network).
acceptance_criteria: REQ-047 AC-1: with a browser guard set (RUNNER_BETA=1 equivalent) and a robots.txt `Sitemap:` line or a URL whose host resolves to 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, makeOutboundFetch / the Spider sitemap seeding / RobotsPolicy.fetch make no connection to that address (injected NetDeps.connect is never called for it).
REQ-047 AC-2: with a browser guard set, a public URL that redirects to a private address is refused at the redirect hop.
REQ-047 AC-3: with no browser guard (local run), the same private-address target is fetched as before (allowPrivate), still pinned to the resolved address.
REQ-047 AC-4: a sitemap `<loc>` or a robots.txt `Sitemap:` line naming another host is logged and skipped, never fetched (fixtures/audit-site/robots.txt has one: sitemaps.example.invalid).
makeOutboundFetch sends GET only, caps the body (an over-cap body still returns its status), and never takes allowPrivate from request input.
access-control contextFetcher sends the context's cookies through makeOutboundFetch with no redirects followed; existing access-control tests still pass unchanged in intent.
No `context.request`, `page.request` or Node `fetch` call remains in deterministic-spider.ts, competitive/robots.ts or access-control.ts.

tasks.title: Checkers take FetchFn only; orchestrator link check and checker fetch on makeOutboundFetch; source-grep guard
tasks.description: ADR 0031 part 2. In packages/checkers: SeoChecker accepts an optional FetchFn (checkPage context or argument); checkBrokenLinks (seo.ts:547-585) sends exactly one GET per link through it (no HEAD then GET), and the Site Root audit (seo.ts:388-410) uses the same FetchFn instead of page.context().request. SecurityDepthChecker: remove defaultFetch (security-depth.ts:43-52) and its fallbacks (:146, :202); with no FetchFn the network checks (security.txt, source maps) make no request and are reported as not checked. Same for broken links and site-root files in SeoChecker. In packages/core: new packages/core/src/checker-fetch.ts with one shared function that builds the checkers' FetchFn for a run (makeOutboundFetch with the run's allowPrivate rule), used by FlowTestOrchestrator and later by the Website Audit analysis (ADR 0033 drift risk, architecture REC-11); orchestrator.ts passes it to securityDepth.checkPage (:1113) and seoChecker.checkPage (:1149); checkLink (:209-221) uses it (one GET, redirects re-checked by safeGet, same 404/410/5xx rule). Add packages/core/tests/outbound-source-grep.test.ts: scans packages/core/src and packages/checkers/src and fails on `context.request`, `page.request`, `request.fetch`, `request.get`/`.head` on a Playwright APIRequestContext, or a Node `fetch(` outside an explicit exception list (AI provider endpoints, preflight.ts, discovery/docs-fetch.ts localDocsGet with the reason 'user-provided address, not page-derived', plan/playwright-export.ts generated code text).
acceptance_criteria: REQ-047 AC-5: SecurityDepthChecker and SeoChecker called without a FetchFn make no network request and report their network checks (security.txt, source maps, broken links, site-root files) as not checked; defaultFetch no longer exists.

tasks.title: robots.txt Crawl-delay and one request at a time per host (host pacer) in Spider and outbound fetch
tasks.description: REQ-035 per Q-12 (accepted ADR 0015 rule: one request at a time per host, robots.txt Crawl-delay honoured) and REQ-034. (1) RobotsPolicy (competitive/robots.ts) parses `Crawl-delay` for the chosen user-agent group and exposes `crawlDelayMs` (absent = undefined; non-numeric or negative ignored; capped at a sane maximum, e.g. 30 s, logged when capped). (2) New packages/core/src/host-pacer.ts: `HostPacer` with `run(host, task)` that allows one in-flight request per host and spaces request starts by max(minGapMs, crawlDelayMs); clock and timer injectable for unit tests. (3) makeOutboundFetch (safe-net.ts) takes an optional `pacer`, so sitemap, robots and checker requests share the host's turn. (4) Deterministic Spider takes an optional `pacer`: when set, every page load to the host and the sitemap/robots fetches wait for its turn (workers never load two pages of one host at once), replacing the shared `waitForPacing` clock for that crawl; existing callers without a pacer keep today's pageDelayMs behaviour. Robots handling (REQ-034) stays at visit time (deterministic-spider.ts:528-534) so a Disallowed URL found by link or in sitemap.xml becomes a Skipped Page with reason `robots`; a missing robots.txt means a normal crawl. The audit crawl (G2) creates one HostPacer per Website Audit from the fetched RobotsPolicy and passes it to the Spider and to every FetchFn it builds.
acceptance_criteria: REQ-034 AC-1: given robots.txt disallows a path for all crawlers, a URL under it met by link (fixture /private/staff-rota) or only in sitemap.xml (fixture /private/reports) is not fetched (absent from the fixture server's request log) and is listed as a Skipped Page with reason `robots`.
REQ-034 AC-2: given no robots.txt (404), the crawl proceeds normally and records no `robots` skips.

REQ-035 AC-1: given Crawl-delay: 1 (fixtures/audit-site/robots.txt), when the Spider crawls with a HostPacer against the fixture server that logs requests, then no two top-level requests to the host (page documents, robots.txt, sitemap files) overlap in time and consecutive starts are at least the Crawl-delay apart.
RobotsPolicy exposes the Crawl-delay of the matching group (specific user-agent first, else `*`); malformed values are ignored.
HostPacer unit tests: one in flight per host, gap respected, different hosts independent, a failing task releases the turn, abort signal stops waiting.
Spider callers that pass no pacer behave exactly as before (existing spider tests unchanged).

tasks.title: Route table access levels, beta policy and :param matching; dispatch closed by default
tasks.description: DEC-001 / REC-06. packages/runner/src/routes/route.ts: `Route` gains required-by-dispatch `access: AuditAccess` (type import from packages/types/src/website-audit.ts: 'owner' | 'view' | 'edit' | 'export' | 'sign-in' | 'public'; no change to the types file) and `beta: 'allow' | 'closed'` (default closed). Paths may contain `:id` / `:linkId` params matched with matchAuditPath (website-audit.ts:1110, which validates AUDIT_ID_PATTERN / SHARE_LINK_ID_PATTERN; a bad id is no match, so a 404); matched params are passed in RouteContext as `params`. Exact rows still beat prefix rows; param rows rank with exact rows in table order. Add a pure `authorizeRoute(route, caller)` returning allow or a refusal (status + code), where caller = { hasAccessKey, beta, helper?: permissions resolver hook }: a route with no access is refused (closed by default); 'owner' needs the access key; 'view'/'edit'/'export' need the access key or a Helper grant with that permission (the Helper resolver is a hook defaulting to 'no Helper'; REQ-033/G6 supplies it); 'sign-in' and 'public' are reachable without the key; in beta (RUNNER_BETA=1) only routes with beta 'allow' are served, and per D-004 (recommended default, parked) audit routes are closed in beta except 'public' Shared Link routes. server.ts dispatch (:902-1015): match the table before grantAccess so 'public'/'sign-in' rows are served without the access key, then apply authorizeRoute; refusals answer JSON `{ error, code }` (401/403) in the existing error model. Existing Plan routes (routes/plan.ts) declare access 'owner' and beta 'allow', keeping today's betaScope/closedInBeta behaviour unchanged. routes/index.ts re-exports authorizeRoute and the new types. Inline endpoints are not migrated in this task (DEC-001 consequence).
acceptance_criteria: REQ-048 AC-1: a route registered without an `access` value is refused at dispatch (unit test on authorizeRoute and a server test with a test-only route table).
REQ-048 AC-3: a route with access `owner` is refused for a request without the owner's access key when RUNNER_ACCESS_TOKEN is set.
REQ-048 AC-4: a route with access `public` (e.g. a `/s/:linkId` test row) is served without the access key, and a malformed linkId does not match (404).
REQ-048 AC-5: with RUNNER_BETA=1, a route whose beta policy is not 'allow' is refused for a beta visitor; a 'public' row with beta 'allow' is served.
`:id` / `:linkId` params match only values meeting AUDIT_ID_PATTERN / SHARE_LINK_ID_PATTERN and reach the handler decoded in RouteContext.params.
Every existing Plan route declares access and beta policy; existing route-table, plan-routes, access-token and beta tests pass with unchanged assertions.
view/edit/export rows accept the owner's access key and consult the Helper resolver hook (default: no Helper), so G6 can add Helper grants without changing dispatch.
